Definition: The share of orders that were delivered by the date the customer was promised.
The share of orders delivered both on the promised date and with the complete quantity ordered -- a stricter version of On-Time Delivery.
Orders that have been placed but not yet completed or shipped.
How long it takes from an order being placed to it being ready or delivered.
The share of ordered items that could be shipped immediately from available stock.
How many times inventory is sold and replaced over a period -- a higher number generally means less cash tied up sitting on shelves.
How many days current inventory would last at the normal rate of use, if nothing more came in.
A commitment to a standard of service -- e.g. how fast an order or request will be handled. An SLA score shows how often that commitment was actually met.
Orders or jobs that are open but haven't yet been assigned a production or delivery slot.

Also known as: Stock; Stock on Hand; Inventory on Hand
Definition: The quantity or value of goods held ready for use or sale.
Occasions when an item is requested but there is none available.
Extra inventory kept as a buffer against uncertainty in demand or supply.
The stock level at which a new order should be placed to avoid running out.
The average number of days inventory is held before it is sold or used.
How many times inventory is sold or used and replaced in a period.

Also known as: Available to Promise; ATP; Free Stock
Definition: The stock that can still be promised to customers, found by taking the stock on hand and removing what is already reserved for orders.

Also known as: Stock Value; Inventory Valuation; Value of Inventory
Definition: The money value of the stock held, normally at cost.
The average amount of stock held over a period, usually found from the opening and closing figures.
How closely the stock records match what is actually counted on the shelves, shown as a percentage.

Also known as: Stock Variance; Stock Count Variance; Count Variance
Definition: The difference between the quantity or value in the records and what was found in a physical count.
Stock lost to theft, damage, errors or spoilage, so that less is found than the records say.

Also known as: Stock to Sales Ratio; Inventory Cover
Definition: How much stock is held compared with sales, showing how many months of sales are covered by the stock on hand.

Also known as: Carrying Cost; Inventory Carrying Cost; Holding Cost
Definition: The cost of keeping stock, including storage, insurance, handling, capital tied up and losses from ageing.
The gross profit earned for each unit of money invested in stock. It shows whether stock is paying its way.

Also known as: Aged Inventory; Stock Ageing; Inventory Aging
Definition: A breakdown of stock by how long it has been held, for example 0 to 30 days or over 180 days.
Stock that sells only in small quantities, so it stays on the shelf for a long time.
Stock that is no longer wanted or can no longer be sold, and which may have to be written off.
Stock held above what is needed to meet expected demand.
The value of stock that has been removed from the books because it is lost, damaged or no longer sellable.

Also known as: Out of Stock Rate; Stock-Out Rate; OOS Rate
Definition: The share of demand, orders or items that could not be met because the stock had run out.
Orders that could not be filled when placed because stock was not available, and are waiting to be supplied.
The share of orders delivered complete, on time, undamaged and with the right documents.
The share of orders sent out with the right items and quantities.
The time taken from receiving an order to having it ready or delivered to the customer.

Also known as: Line Fill Rate; Line Item Fill Rate
Definition: The share of order lines that were shipped in full from stock.
How closely the forecast of demand matched what customers actually ordered.
How much demand moves up and down from period to period. Higher variability needs more safety stock.

Also known as: Vendor Lead Time; Procurement Lead Time
Definition: The time between placing an order with a supplier and receiving the goods.
How much the time it takes to receive goods changes from order to order. A steady lead time is easier to plan around.

Also known as: Vendor OTD; Supplier Delivery Performance; Supplier OTD
Definition: The share of supplier deliveries that arrived on or before the promised date.
The share of ordered quantities that the supplier delivered.

Also known as: Incoming Quality; Supplier Defect Rate; Vendor Quality
Definition: The share of goods received from a supplier that passed inspection.
The number of days between paying suppliers for materials and being paid by customers for the finished goods.
The average number of days the business takes to pay its suppliers.

Also known as: Supply Chain Cost; Cost to Serve; Supply Chain Spend
Definition: The sum of all costs of buying, making, storing and delivering goods, shown in total or as a percentage of sales.

Also known as: Logistics Cost to Sales; Distribution Cost
Definition: The cost of storing and moving goods, shown in total or as a percentage of sales.

Also known as: Transportation Cost; Shipping Cost; Freight Spend
Definition: The money spent on moving goods by road, sea, air or rail.

Also known as: Transport Cost per Unit; Shipping Cost per Unit
Definition: The freight cost divided by the number of units moved.
The share of shipments collected from the warehouse or supplier at the agreed time.
The share of orders that left the warehouse on or before the planned dispatch date.

Also known as: Transit Time; Delivery Time; Shipping Lead Time
Definition: The time between an order leaving the warehouse and arriving at the customer.

Also known as: Shipping Damage Rate; Freight Damage Rate; Transit Damage
Definition: The share of shipments or items that arrived damaged.

Also known as: Truck Fill Rate; Vehicle Fill Rate; Load Factor
Definition: How much of a vehicle's capacity was used on a trip. A fuller load means a lower cost per unit moved.

Also known as: Warehouse Utilization; Space Utilisation; Storage Utilization
Definition: The share of the warehouse's storage space that is in use.

Also known as: Lines Picked per Hour; Picks per Hour; Pick Rate
Definition: The number of items or order lines picked for each hour of labour.
The time between goods arriving at the dock and being available to pick in stock.
The share of goods receipts where the quantity and item received match the order and delivery note.
The order size that gives the lowest combined cost of ordering and holding stock.
The smallest amount that a supplier will agree to sell in one order.

Also known as: Replenishment Frequency; Number of Orders Placed
Definition: How often orders are placed with suppliers for an item or a group of items.
The time taken to bring stock back up to its target level after a need is identified.

Also known as: Min Max; Minimum and Maximum Stock
Definition: The lowest and highest stock levels set for an item. Stock is ordered when it falls to the minimum, up to the maximum.
How many days of average demand the safety stock can cover.

Also known as: Weeks of Cover; Weeks of Supply; Days of Cover
Definition: How long the stock on hand would last at the current rate of sales or use.
The share of goods received that were sent back to the supplier.

Also known as: Returns Handling Cost; Returns Processing Cost
Definition: The cost of taking back, checking and re-stocking or disposing of returned goods.
A score showing how exposed the supply chain is to disruptions such as supplier failure, delays or shortages.

Also known as: Single Source Items; Sole Source Dependency
Definition: The share of items that can be bought from only one supplier, which makes supply fragile.
